title: Out-of-State Owners
metaTitle: Sell Wyoming Mineral Rights From Out of State
metaDescription: Live outside Wyoming but own minerals here? We buy interests from absentee owners entirely by mail and phone, no trip to a county courthouse required.
heroLead: You don't have to live in Wyoming, or ever have, to hold minerals here, and you don't have to fly in to sell them either. We close with owners in every part of the country by mail and phone.
intro: A surprising share of Wyoming mineral owners have never set foot in the county where their interest sits. The minerals passed down from a relative who homesteaded or ranched here generations ago, and the family scattered to other states while the interest stayed on the books in Campbell, Sublette, Sweetwater, Laramie, or wherever the original deed was filed.

That distance creates real friction. Royalty checks get mailed to an outdated address. Lease offers arrive by certified mail with a deadline and nobody local to ask about them. Property tax notices, if applicable, go to a forwarding address that eventually stops working. None of that is your fault, but it's the kind of thing that piles up when the asset and the owner are a thousand miles apart.

sections.heading: Managing a Wyoming Interest From Somewhere Else
paragraphs: There's no requirement that a mineral owner live near the property, and plenty of Wyoming production is owned by people in Texas, California, the Midwest, and everywhere in between. But managing it well from a distance means staying current on operator changes, keeping your mailing address updated with every company that might send a division order, and tracking lease offers that show up unpredictably.

Most absentee owners we talk to have fallen behind on at least one of those, usually not from neglect but because there was never a clear reason to prioritize it. A check for forty dollars a month doesn't usually justify the time it would take to fully understand what you own and what it's worth.

sections.heading: Selling Without Traveling to Wyoming
paragraphs: We handle the entire process by mail, phone, and email. You don't need to visit the county courthouse yourself — we pull the title records directly. You don't need to meet in person to sign; closing documents can be notarized wherever you live and returned by mail. We've closed with sellers who've never seen the acreage their family has owned for eighty years, and that's completely normal.

The one thing that speeds this up on your end is having whatever paperwork you do have handy — an old deed, a royalty statement, a lease, even a family letter that mentions the property. If you don't have any of that, the county and a rough sense of where the property is located is usually enough for us to start.

sections.heading: Why Out-of-State Owners Often Choose to Sell
paragraphs: For owners who never plan to live near the minerals or get more involved in managing them, converting a distant, low-touch asset into a single payment is often more useful than continuing to track small checks and occasional mail from operators you've never spoken with. It's one less thing tied to a state you may have no other connection to anymore.

That's not the right call for everyone. Some absentee owners are happy holding a producing interest as passive income regardless of distance. We're not going to push you toward selling if the current arrangement works fine for your family. We just make sure distance itself isn't the reason a fair transaction doesn't happen.

sections.heading: What We Need From You
paragraphs: Send us the county and legal description if you have it, along with any deed, lease, or royalty paperwork on hand. We'll pull the rest from Wyoming county records and come back with a written offer and a straightforward closing process that doesn't require you to leave your home state.
If you're not sure what county your family's minerals are even in, that's a common starting point too. Old family paperwork, even incomplete, is usually enough for us to trace it.

sections.heading: When the Family Land Feels Like Someone Else's State
paragraphs: For heirs who've never visited Wyoming and have no plans to, a mineral interest here can feel less like an asset and more like an obligation attached to a place they don't otherwise think about. That's a completely understandable position, and it's often the deciding factor for out-of-state owners who choose to sell rather than continue managing something disconnected from the rest of their life.

Other families keep the connection deliberately, treating a small Wyoming royalty check as a tie to where a grandparent or great-grandparent once lived and worked. Either choice is reasonable. We just make sure the distance itself never becomes the reason a fair deal doesn't happen.

faqs.question: Do I have to travel to Wyoming to sell my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No. We handle the entire process remotely by mail, phone, and email, including notarized closing documents sent wherever you live.

faqs.question: I've lost track of which county my family's minerals are in. Can you help?
faqs.answer: Yes. Send whatever old paperwork or family information you have, and we can often trace the property through Wyoming county records.

faqs.question: Is it harder to sell an out-of-state interest than one owned locally?
faqs.answer: Not for us. Location of the owner doesn't affect what your minerals are worth. We evaluate the property itself, wherever you happen to live.

faqs.question: How do closing documents work if I'm not in Wyoming?
faqs.answer: Documents can be notarized at your local bank, UPS store, or notary service and returned to us by mail. We coordinate the timing so nothing gets held up.

faqs.question: Should I update my mailing address with the operator even if I plan to sell?
faqs.answer: It doesn't hurt, but if you're selling, the buyer will handle updating ownership records going forward, so it's not essential before a sale closes.
